=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:13918-13930 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The case statement that records failure conclusions was moved inside the `if` block. In the original code, the case ran unconditionally after the `if` (with `break` on failure). In the new code, the case only runs when the timestamp comparison passes. This creates an asymmetric tie-breaker: if the first iteration of `wf_candidate` is a `success` at timestamp T and a later iteration is a `failure` at the same timestamp T, the failure is not recorded. The tie-breaker condition `[ -n "${_rtr_failed_conclusion}" ] && [ "${_rtr_wf_conclusion}" = "success" ]` only fires when a prior iteration already set `_rtr_failed_conclusion`, so a success-then-failure sequence at the same timestamp leaves `_rtr_failed_conclusion` empty throughout.
  WHY: With `_rtr_failed_conclusion` empty, `retrigger_review_inline` will not redispatch the review for a PR whose newest review run failed at the same timestamp as a prior success. The poller will fall through to the empty-commit push guard, clobbering the live review run with an empty commit (the exact failure mode the original `break` prevented). This regression specifically affects the `internal-review.yml` and `review_autofix.yml` candidates that follow `ai-review.yml` in the iteration order when their runs share a timestamp with the prior success.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:12030-12045 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test sets `active_autofix_runs` to model the pending dispatch run, but `_has_active_autofix_run` (the function the conflict sweep calls) reaches the PR-named dispatch run via `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs`, which calls `gh api` against the `actions/workflows/<wrapper>/runs` endpoint. That endpoint is mocked by the `actions_runs_workflow_runs` fixture (see lines 12372, 17201, 17264, 17268), not by `active_autofix_runs`. Without an `actions_runs_workflow_runs=[...]` entry for the pending `Internal: AI Review & Autofix [pr:411]` run, the mock returns an empty list and `_pr_named_review_dispatch_runs` returns `[]`, so `_has_active_autofix_run` returns 1 (no active run), the conflict sweep dispatches, and `result["review_dispatches"]` becomes non-empty — failing both assertions.
  WHY: The test does not exercise the production path it claims to verify. The first assertion (`result["review_dispatches"] == []`) will fail because a redundant dispatch was issued. The second assertion (`"Active autofix run found" in result["stdout"]`) will fail because no active-run log line was emitted. The test passes only if `actions_runs_workflow_runs` is supplied for the `internal-review.yml` wrapper with the matching `display_title` and `pending` status, mirroring the pattern already used at line 12372 in `test_standalone_retrigger_review_sees_pr_named_pending_run`.
